sanskrit: sa cāpi pāpaprakṛtir daiteyāpasado nṛpa mayy avarṣata durdharṣaḥ śaradhārāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: That evil-natured outcast of the demons, O king, formidable as he was, poured upon me torrents of arrows by the thousands.

sanskrit: sainikān mama sūtaṃ ca hayāṃś ca samavākirat acintayantas tu śarān vayaṃ yudhyāma bhārata
english: He showered arrows upon my soldiers, my charioteer, and my horses; yet we fought on, O Bharata, paying no heed to his shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasrāṇi śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām cikṣipuḥ samare vīrā mayi śālvapadānugāḥ
english: Then the warriors who followed Shalva's standard hurled upon me in battle hundreds of thousands of well-notched arrows.

sanskrit: te hayān me rathaṃ caiva tadā dārukam eva ca chādayām āsur asurā bāṇair marmavibhedibhiḥ
english: Those demons covered my horses, my chariot, and Daruka himself with arrows that pierced to the vital points.

sanskrit: na hayā na ratho vīra na yantā mama dārukaḥ adṛśyanta śaraiś channās tathāhaṃ sainikāś ca me
english: O hero, neither the horses nor the chariot nor my charioteer Daruka could be seen, hidden as they were beneath those arrows; nor could I myself be seen, nor my soldiers.

sanskrit: tato 'ham api kauravya śarāṇām ayutān bahūn abhimantritānāṃ dhanuṣā divyena vidhinākṣipam
english: Then I too, O Kauravya, duly discharged with my divine bow many tens of thousands of arrows that had been consecrated with mantras.

sanskrit: na tatra viṣayas tv āsīn mama sainyasya bhārata khe viṣaktaṃ hi tat saubhaṃ krośamātra ivābhavat
english: But that Saubha, suspended in the sky, was out of reach of my army, O Bharata — it hovered at a distance of barely a krośa.

sanskrit: tatas te prekṣakāḥ sarve raṅgavāṭa iva sthitāḥ harṣayām āsur uccair māṃ siṃhanādatalasvanaiḥ
english: Then all those onlookers, standing as though in an arena, cheered me loudly with lion-roars and clapping of hands.

sanskrit: matkārmukavinirmuktā dānavānāṃ mahāraṇe aṅgeṣu rudhirāktās te viviśuḥ śalabhā iva
english: The arrows discharged from my bow entered the bodies of the demons in that great battle, stained with blood, like locusts swarming in.

sanskrit: tato halahalāśabdaḥ saubhamadhye vyavardhata vadhyatāṃ viśikhais tīkṣṇaiḥ patatāṃ ca mahārṇave
english: Then a great tumult arose within Saubha as those struck by my sharp arrows fell into the vast ocean.

sanskrit: te nikṛttabhujaskandhāḥ kabandhākṛtidarśanāḥ nadanto bhairavān nādan nipatanti sma dānavāḥ
english: Those demons, their arms and shoulders severed, looking like headless trunks, roaring fearful roars, fell down.

sanskrit: tato gokṣīrakundendumṛṇālarajataprabham jalajaṃ pāñcajanyaṃ vai prāṇenāham apūrayam
english: Then I filled with my breath the Panchajanya — that conch born of the waters, bright as cow's milk, white jasmine, the moon, lotus stalks, and silver.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā patitāṃs tatra śālvaḥ saubhapatis tadā māyāyuddhena mahatā yodhayām āsa māṃ yudhi
english: Seeing them fallen, Shalva, the lord of Saubha, then began to fight against me in battle with a great magical warfare.

sanskrit: tato huḍahuḍāḥ prāsāḥ śaktiśūlaparaśvadhāḥ paṭṭiśāś ca bhuśuṇḍyaś ca prāpatann aniśaṃ mayi
english: Then javelins, spears, tridents, battle-axes, double-edged swords, and fire-tubes rained down upon me ceaselessly.

sanskrit: tān ahaṃ māyayaivāśu pratigṛhya vyanāśayam tasyāṃ hatāyāṃ māyāyāṃ giriśṛṅgair ayodhayat
english: I quickly countered all of those with my own magic and destroyed them; when that illusion was shattered, he fought me with mountain peaks.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavat tama iva prabhātam iva cābhavat durdinaṃ sudinaṃ caiva śītam uṣṇaṃ ca bhārata
english: Then it seemed like darkness, then again like dawn; it seemed a bad day, then a fair one; cold, then hot, O Bharata.

sanskrit: evaṃ māyāṃ vikurvāṇo yodhayām āsa māṃ ripuḥ vijñāya tad ahaṃ sarvaṃ māyayaiva vyanāśayam yathākālaṃ tu yuddhena vyadhamaṃ sarvataḥ śaraiḥ
english: Thus the enemy fought against me, deploying illusion after illusion; knowing all of it, I destroyed each illusion with my own, and then at the proper moment scattered him on all sides with arrows in direct combat.

sanskrit: tato vyoma mahārāja śatasūryam ivābhavat śatacandraṃ ca kaunteya sahasrāyutatārakam
english: Then the sky, O great king, appeared as if lit by a hundred suns, a hundred moons, and thousands upon ten-thousands of stars, O son of Kunti.

sanskrit: tato nājñāyata tadā divārātraṃ tathā diśaḥ tato 'haṃ moham āpannaḥ prajñāstraṃ samayojayam tatas tad astram astreṇa vidhūtaṃ śaratūlavat
english: Then neither day nor night could be distinguished, nor the directions; overcome with bewilderment, I applied the Prajñā weapon, and by means of that weapon the illusion was scattered like cotton by the wind.

sanskrit: tathā tad abhavad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam labdhālokaś ca rājendra punaḥ śatrum ayodhayam
english: Such was that tumultuous, hair-raising battle; and once light was restored, O lord of kings, I fought the enemy again.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca evaṃ sa puruṣavyāghra śālvo rājñāṃ mahāripuḥ yudhyamāno mayā saṃkhye viyad abhyāgamat punaḥ
english: Vasudeva said: Thus fighting with me in battle, O tiger among men, Shalva, that great enemy of kings, once again rose into the sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ śataghnīś ca mahāgadāś ca; dīptāṃś ca śūlān musalān asīṃś ca cikṣepa roṣān mayi mandabuddhiḥ; śālvo mahārāja jayābhikāṅkṣī
english: Then Shalva, that dull-witted one, craving victory, hurled at me in fury, O great king, śataghnis, great maces, blazing tridents, pestles, and swords.

sanskrit: tān āśugair āpatato 'ham āśu; nivārya tūrṇaṃ khagamān kha eva dvidhā tridhā cācchinam āśu muktais; tato 'ntarikṣe ninado babhūva
english: I quickly repelled those weapons as they came hurtling at me, and with arrows swiftly released I cut them in two and three pieces right there in the sky; then a great noise arose in the atmosphere.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasreṇa śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām dārukaṃ vājinaś caiva rathaṃ ca samavākirat
english: Then with a hundred thousand well-notched arrows he covered Daruka, the horses, and the chariot.

sanskrit: tato mām abravīd vīra dāruko vihvalann iva sthātavyam iti tiṣṭhāmi śālvabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ
english: Then Daruka spoke to me, O hero, seeming distressed: "I can barely hold my place here, tormented as I am by Shalva's arrows."

sanskrit: iti tasya niśamyāhaṃ sāratheḥ karuṇaṃ vacaḥ avekṣamāṇo yantāram apaśyaṃ śarapīḍitam
english: Hearing those pitiful words from my charioteer, I turned to look at him and saw him pierced and tormented by arrows.

sanskrit: na tasyorasi no mūrdhni na kāye na bhujadvaye antaraṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha paśyāmi nahataṃ śaraiḥ
english: O foremost of the Pandavas, I could see not a single spot on his chest, his head, his body, or his two arms that had not been struck by arrows.

sanskrit: sa tu bāṇavarotpīḍād visravaty asṛg ulbaṇam abhivṛṣṭo yathā meghair girir gairikadhātumān
english: From the torment of that arrow-shower, copious blood streamed from him, like a mountain rich with ochre ore drenched by clouds.

sanskrit: abhīṣuhastaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā sīdantaṃ sārathiṃ raṇe astambhayaṃ mahābāho śālvabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ
english: Seeing that charioteer, reins still in hand, sinking in battle, tormented by Shalva's arrows, I steadied him, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: atha māṃ puruṣaḥ kaś cid dvārakānilayo 'bravīt tvarito ratham abhyetya sauhṛdād iva bhārata
english: Then a certain man from Dvaraka came hurrying to my chariot and spoke to me, as if out of friendship, O Bharata.

sanskrit: āhukasya vaco vīra tasyaiva paricārakaḥ viṣaṇṇaḥ sannakaṇṭho vai tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: He was an attendant of Ahuka, O hero, downcast and choked with sorrow — hear what he said, O Yudhishthira.

sanskrit: dvārakādhipatir vīra āha tvām āhuko vacaḥ keśaveha vijānīṣva yat tvāṃ pitṛsakho 'bravīt
english: "The lord of Dvaraka, Ahuka, sends you this message, O hero — understand it well, O Keshava, hear what your father's friend says to you.

sanskrit: upayātvādya śālvena dvārakāṃ vṛṣṇinandana viṣakte tvayi durdharṣa hataḥ śūrasuto balāt
english: 'Shalva has attacked Dvaraka today, O joy of the Vrishnis; while you were engaged elsewhere, O invincible one, the son of Shura has been slain by force.'

sanskrit: tad alaṃ sādhu yuddhena nivartasva janārdana dvārakām eva rakṣasva kāryam etan mahat tava
english: 'Therefore, enough of this battle; turn back, O Janardana; protect Dvaraka itself — that is the great duty before you now.'

sanskrit: ity ahaṃ tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā paramadurmanāḥ niścayaṃ nādhigacchāmi kartavyasyetarasya vā
english: Hearing those words of his, I became extremely distressed and could not settle on what was to be done or what was not.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ baladevaṃ ca pradyumnaṃ ca mahāratham jagarhe manasā vīra tac chrutvā vipriyaṃ vacaḥ
english: Hearing those unwelcome words, O hero, I inwardly reproached Satyaki, Balarama, and the great warrior Pradyumna in my mind.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi dvārakāyāś ca pituś ca kurunandana teṣu rakṣāṃ samādhāya prayātaḥ saubhapātane
english: For I had entrusted to them, O joy of the Kurus, the protection of Dvaraka and of my father before setting out to destroy Saubha.

sanskrit: baladevo mahābāhuḥ kaccij jīvati śatruhā sātyakī raukmiṇeyaś ca cārudeṣṇaś ca vīryavān sāmbaprabhṛtayaś caivety aham āsaṃ sudurmanāḥ
english: 'Does the mighty-armed Balarama, slayer of foes, still live? And Satyaki? And Rukminī's son? And the valiant Charudeshna? And Samba and the rest?' — thinking thus, I was overcome with deep grief.

sanskrit: eteṣu hi naravyāghra jīvatsu na kathaṃ cana śakyaḥ śūrasuto hantum api vajrabhṛtā svayam
english: For while these tiger-like men are alive, not even Indra himself, wielder of the thunderbolt, could slay the son of Shura.

sanskrit: hataḥ śūrasuto vyaktaṃ vyaktaṃ te ca parāsavaḥ baladevamukhāḥ sarve iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: The son of Shura must clearly be slain, and clearly Balarama and all the rest must also be dead — so my mind was convinced.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ sarvavināśaṃ taṃ cintayāno muhur muhuḥ suvihvalo mahārāja punaḥ śālvam ayodhayam
english: And I, repeatedly brooding over that total ruin, utterly shaken, O great king, fought Shalva again.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyaṃ mahārāja prapatantam ahaṃ tadā saubhāc chūrasutaṃ vīra tato māṃ moha āviśat
english: Then I saw, O great king, the son of Shura falling down from Saubha, O hero; thereupon bewilderment seized me.

sanskrit: tasya rūpaṃ prapatataḥ pitur mama narādhipa yayāteḥ kṣīṇapuṇyasya svargād iva mahītalam
english: As he fell, the form of my father, O lord of men, was like that of Yayati when his merit was exhausted and he fell from heaven to earth.

sanskrit: viśīrṇagalitoṣṇīṣaḥ prakīrṇāmbaramūrdhajaḥ prapatan dṛśyate ha sma kṣīṇapuṇya iva grahaḥ
english: His turban fallen and disheveled, his garments and hair scattered, he appeared as he fell like a planet whose merit is spent.

sanskrit: tataḥ śārṅgaṃ dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ karāt prapatitaṃ mama mohāt sannaś ca kaunteya rathopastha upāviśam
english: Then the Sharnga, best of bows, fell from my hands in that delusion, and overcome, O son of Kunti, I sank down onto the floor of the chariot.

sanskrit: tato hāhākṛtaṃ sarvaṃ sainyaṃ me gatacetanam māṃ dṛṣṭvā rathanīḍasthaṃ gatāsum iva bhārata
english: Then all my army cried out in dismay, losing their senses, seeing me slumped in the chariot-seat as if dead, O Bharata.

sanskrit: prasārya bāhū patataḥ prasārya caraṇāv api rūpaṃ pitur apaśyaṃ tac chakuneḥ patato yathā
english: Arms outstretched, feet outstretched as he fell — I saw that form of my father like a bird in flight falling down.

sanskrit: taṃ patantaṃ mahābāho śūlapaṭṭiśapāṇayaḥ abhighnanto bhṛśaṃ vīrā mama ceto vyakampayan
english: O mighty-armed one, those warriors, spears and swords in hand, striking him hard as he fell, caused my heart to tremble violently.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtāt pratilabhya saṃjñām; ahaṃ tadā vīra mahāvimarde na tatra saubhaṃ na ripuṃ na śālvaṃ; paśyāmi vṛddhaṃ pitaraṃ na cāpi
english: Then after a moment, regaining my senses, O hero, in that great tumult I could see neither Saubha nor the enemy nor Shalva — nor the aged form of my father.

sanskrit: tato mamāsīn manasi māyeyam iti niścitam prabuddho 'smi tato bhūyaḥ śataśo vikirañ śarān
english: Then my mind settled with certainty: this is illusion. Fully awakened, I once again scattered arrows by the hundreds.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca tato 'haṃ bharataśreṣṭha pragṛhya ruciraṃ dhanuḥ śarair apātayaṃ saubhāc chirāṃsi vibudhadviṣām
english: Vasudeva said: Then, O best of Bharatas, grasping my splendid bow, I brought down with arrows the heads of those enemies of the gods from Saubha.

sanskrit: śarāṃś cāśīviṣākārān ūrdhvagāṃs tigmatejasaḥ apraiṣaṃ śālvarājāya śārṅgamuktān suvāsasaḥ
english: And I sent upward-flying arrows like venomous serpents, of fierce brilliance, released from the Sharnga with full draw, toward the king Shalva.

sanskrit: tato nādṛśyata tadā saubhaṃ kurukulodvaha antarhitaṃ māyayābhūt tato 'haṃ vismito 'bhavam
english: Then Saubha was no longer visible, O foremost of the Kuru line — it had vanished by illusion; and I was filled with wonder.

sanskrit: atha dānavasaṃghās te vikṛtānanamūrdhajāḥ udakrośan mahārāja viṣṭhite mayi bhārata
english: Then those hosts of demons, with distorted faces and wild hair, screamed out, O great king, while I stood firm, O Bharata.

sanskrit: tato 'straṃ śabdasāhaṃ vai tvaramāṇo mahāhave ayojayaṃ tadvadhāya tataḥ śabda upāramat
english: Then I quickly applied in that great battle the weapon that tracks sound, for the purpose of killing them; thereupon the sound ceased.

sanskrit: hatās te dānavāḥ sarve yaiḥ sa śabda udīritaḥ śarair ādityasaṃkāśair jvalitaiḥ śabdasādhanaiḥ
english: All those demons who had raised that cry were slain by flaming arrows bright as the sun, guided by sound.

sanskrit: tasminn uparate śabde punar evānyato 'bhavat śabdo 'paro mahārāja tatrāpi prāharaṃ śarān
english: When that sound ceased, another cry arose from a different direction, O great king; there too I struck with arrows.

sanskrit: evaṃ daśa diśaḥ sarvās tiryag ūrdhvaṃ ca bhārata nādayām āsur asurās te cāpi nihatā mayā
english: Thus the demons made their cries from all ten directions, sideways and upward too, O Bharata — and all of them were slain by me.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāgjyotiṣaṃ gatvā punar eva vyadṛśyata saubhaṃ kāmagamaṃ vīra mohayan mama cakṣuṣī
english: Then Saubha, that city that moved at will, having gone to the east, appeared again, O hero, bewildering my eyes.

sanskrit: tato lokāntakaraṇo dānavo vānarākṛtiḥ śilāvarṣeṇa sahasā mahatā māṃ samāvṛṇot
english: Then a demon of monkey-like form, a destroyer of worlds, suddenly overwhelmed me with a great shower of stones.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ parvatavarṣeṇa vadhyamānaḥ samantataḥ valmīka iva rājendra parvatopacito 'bhavam
english: Struck on all sides by that shower of mountain rocks, O lord of kings, I became like an anthill heaped up with mountain stones.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ parvatacitaḥ sahayaḥ sahasārathiḥ aprakhyātim iyāṃ rājan sadhvajaḥ parvataiś citaḥ
english: Then I, with my horses, charioteer, and banner, buried under mountains, O king, became invisible, covered by those rocks.

sanskrit: tato vṛṣṇipravīrā ye mamāsan sainikās tadā te bhayārtā diśaḥ sarvāḥ sahasā vipradudruvuḥ
english: Then those Vrishni heroes who were my soldiers, seized with terror, suddenly fled in all directions.

sanskrit: tato hāhākṛtaṃ sarvam abhūt kila viśāṃ pate dyauś ca bhūmiś ca khaṃ caivādṛśyamāne tathā mayi
english: Then there arose a universal cry of dismay, O lord of peoples — heaven, earth, and sky all cried out when I became invisible.

sanskrit: tato viṣaṇṇamanaso mama rājan suhṛjjanāḥ ruruduś cukruśuś caiva duḥkhaśokasamanvitāḥ
english: Then my well-wishing friends, their hearts sunk with grief, O king, wept and wailed, overcome with pain and sorrow.

sanskrit: dviṣatāṃ ca praharṣo 'bhūd ārtiś cādviṣatām api evaṃ vijitavān vīra paścād aśrauṣam acyuta
english: The enemies rejoiced, and even those who were not enemies felt anguish; so did things stand, O hero — I heard of all this afterward, O Achyuta.

sanskrit: tato 'ham astraṃ dayitaṃ sarvapāṣāṇabhedanam vajram udyamya tān sarvān parvatān samaśātayam
english: Then, taking up my beloved Vajra weapon, the crusher of all stones, I shattered all those mountains to pieces.

sanskrit: tataḥ parvatabhārārtā mandaprāṇaviceṣṭitāḥ hayā mama mahārāja vepamānā ivābhavan
english: Then my horses, crushed under the weight of those mountains, moved feebly with labored breath, O great king, trembling as it were.

sanskrit: meghajālam ivākāśe vidāryābhyuditaṃ ravim dṛṣṭvā māṃ bāndhavāḥ sarve harṣam āhārayan punaḥ
english: Seeing me emerge like the sun rising and splitting apart a mass of clouds in the sky, all my kinsmen rejoiced again.

sanskrit: tato mām abravīt sūtaḥ prāñjaliḥ praṇato nṛpa sādhu saṃpaśya vārṣṇeya śālvaṃ saubhapatiṃ sthitam
english: Then my charioteer, folding his hands and bowing, said to me, O king: 'Look well, O descendant of Vrishni — Shalva, the lord of Saubha, stands before you.'

sanskrit: alaṃ kṛṣṇāvamanyainaṃ sādhu yatnaṃ samācara mārdavaṃ sakhitāṃ caiva śālvād adya vyapāhara
english: 'Enough of disdaining him, O Krishna — apply yourself earnestly; abandon all gentleness and friendship toward Shalva today.'

sanskrit: jahi śālvaṃ mahābāho mainaṃ jīvaya keśava sarvaiḥ parākramair vīra vadhyaḥ śatrur amitrahan
english: 'Slay Shalva, O mighty-armed one; do not let him live, O Keshava; with all your valor, O hero, the enemy is to be killed, O destroyer of foes.'

sanskrit: na śatrur avamantavyo durbalo 'pi balīyasā yo 'pi syāt pīṭhagaḥ kaś cit kiṃ punaḥ samare sthitaḥ
english: 'An enemy must not be despised, even a weak one by the strong — how much less one who is standing firm in battle?'

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla sarvayatnair imaṃ prabho jahi vṛṣṇikulaśreṣṭha mā tvāṃ kālo 'tyagāt punaḥ
english: 'Therefore, O tiger among men, O master, O best of the Vrishni clan, slay him with all your efforts — do not let the right moment pass you by again.'

sanskrit: naiṣa mārdavasādhyo vai mato nāpi sakhā tava yena tvaṃ yodhito vīra dvārakā cāvamarditā
english: 'He is not to be won over by gentleness, nor is he your friend — he who has fought you, O hero, and laid waste to Dvaraka.'

sanskrit: evamādi tu kaunteya śrutvāhaṃ sārather vacaḥ tattvam etad iti jñātvā yuddhe matim adhārayam
english: Hearing such words from my charioteer, O son of Kunti, recognizing their truth, I fixed my mind firmly on battle.

sanskrit: vadhāya śālvarājasya saubhasya ca nipātane dārukaṃ cābruvaṃ vīra muhūrtaṃ sthīyatām iti
english: For the slaying of king Shalva and the bringing down of Saubha, I said to Daruka, O hero: 'Hold your position for a moment.'

sanskrit: tato 'pratihataṃ divyam abhedyam ativīryavat āgneyam astraṃ dayitaṃ sarvasāhaṃ mahāprabham
english: Then the divine, irresistible, impenetrable, supremely powerful, beloved Agneya weapon, bearer of all things, of great blazing splendor —

sanskrit: yakṣāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca dānavānāṃ ca saṃyuge rājñāṃ ca pratilomānāṃ bhasmāntakaraṇaṃ mahat
english: — that great weapon, the reducer to ash of Yakshas, Rakshasas, demons, and wicked kings in battle —

sanskrit: kṣurāntam amalaṃ cakraṃ kālāntakayamopamam abhimantryāham atulaṃ dviṣatāṃ ca nibarhaṇam
english: — I consecrated with mantras the immaculate discus with razor edge, incomparable, the destroyer of enemies, like Yama the Ender of time itself.
